proposed statement: Parents struggle to get information from the school because fee statements are printed and sent home in learner's bags but half never reach parents
key statement: SchoolBase 7 (from about 2014) runs on a server in the admin block. It holds learners, parents, fees and marks, exports CSV, produces the report PDFs, and sends the emails.

proposed statement: The portal must allow parents to report their child's absence with reason and dates, visible to the class teacher and office immediately
key statement: Parents submit an absence note (reason and dates) in the portal, and the class teacher and the office both see it straight away.

proposed statement: The portal must deliver school notices from the office and grade heads to parents
key statement: The office and grade heads send notices to the whole school, one grade or one team.

proposed statement: The portal must be zero-rated by the network to help parents with expensive data costs
key statement: Could the portal be zero-rated with the mobile networks? The consultant will look into it.

proposed statement: The portal must support Isizulu language and large, clear text for users with visual impairments
key statement: Use the school's maroon, not a generic blue.

proposed statement: The portal must use the school's maroon color scheme instead of generic blue
key statement: Use the school's maroon, not a generic blue.

proposed statement: The client has only one IT person who works two days a week, leading to potential unavailability during report nights
key statement: The school has one IT person, two days a week; if something breaks on report night, there is nobody.

proposed statement: The portal must allow parents to view Term 2 reports by June 26
key statement: Parents should get the term-two reports (out on 26 June) through the portal.

proposed statement: The client wants to trial the portal with Grade 8 term 1 reports in April before full rollout
key statement: Trial the portal with grade 8's term-one reports in April before the full roll-out, so a bad first report day doesn't cost parents' trust.

proposed statement: A risk is that poor performance of the first report day could lead to immediate loss of parent trust in the portal
key statement: Trial the portal with grade 8's term-one reports in April before the full roll-out, so a bad first report day doesn't cost parents' trust.

proposed statement: The client uses school base to manage parent contacts, which has 1,650 parent contacts
key statement: On report day every parent logs in within a couple of hours, mostly in the evening, from about 1,650 parent contacts (corrected from 1,400). Last year a one-grade test of reports on the website took the site down.
